result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. Riley got 3 items correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model only outputs a request naming the tool and its arguments. In s1 you picked the option saying the model opens the booking system itself, so this is an improvement. |
| q3 | Wrong (M6) | You picked "it will eventually fix the bug". An agent that repeats the same failing step 40 times needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. You answered this correctly in s1. |
| q4 | Partial (M4) | The count of 4 is right. Your reasoning says the model runs the tools itself, but the program runs them and the model only requests them. |
| q5 | Correct | The result goes back as the model's next input so it can decide what to do next. |
| q6 | Partial | The model picks a tool from its full description (name, purpose, parameters), not from the name alone. |

**Summary:** You have the loop, what the model outputs for a tool call, and what happens to a tool's result. The belief that the model runs the tools itself is still showing in q4. q3 also needs work on stopping a loop that keeps repeating itself.

**Next step:** Trace the laser-cutter request on paper, with "model output" and "program action" as separate lines for each of the four calls. Mark where a step limit would go. After that we can move on to context and memory.

I also added `learning-records/0003-who-runs-the-tool-and-when-to-stop.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `s1` is still ungraded; I can grade it if you want to compare the two attempts.
